methods.rationale: 9 same-sector peers exist in Climate & Energy, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in Climate & Bio-Manufacturing

data.narrative:
Endurance Energy is a SPAC-stage climate and energy company founded by Andrew Redd, having raised $5M+ to date. The valuation exercise operates within a fragmented peer universe: nine private companies in Climate & Energy exist, alongside one public comparable (LNZA). The private peer set includes later-stage ventures such as Helion, Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, and Electric Hydrogen.

Peer-median triangulation is not applicable here. The Climate & Energy sector lacks a sufficient cohort of same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables with similar valuation tiers—zero datapoints met the threshold of three or more peers necessary for reliable median pricing. While nine same-sector peers exist, their heterogeneity across stage, technology, and capitalization prevents meaningful cross-sectional analysis. A sector-wide median would introduce material distortion given the wide dispersion between pre-revenue frontier technologies and more mature ventures within the Climate & Energy universe.

No triangulated valuation range can be supported by the data provided. Further analysis would require either: (i) expansion to adjacent sectors with similar-stage characteristics; (ii) cash-flow or comparable-transaction analysis if such data becomes available; or (iii) explicit disclosure of SPAC merger terms if applicable. The primary valuation uncertainty stems from stage-specific risk and the absence of narrow peer anchors. At present, only the $5M+ raised to date offers a direct empirical floor for analysis.
